text: Data Structure. An organisation of data for efficient access and modification.
Graph. A graph is a set of vertices connected by edges. Is a kind of: Data Structure.
Graph Database. A database optimised for storing and querying graph-structured data with native traversal. Is a kind of: Data Structure. Relations — contrastsWith: Vector Database.

Knowledge Graph. A knowledge graph represents entities and their relationships as a typed graph with formal semantics, enabling reasoning and structured retrieval. Is a kind of: Graph. Relations — hasPart: Ontology; uses: urn:ngm:class:graph database. Knowledge graphs fuse a schema-level ontology with instance-level assertions, so a query can traverse typed edges and a reasoner can derive facts that were never asserted — the "semantic" half of the semantic web.
Ontology. A formal, explicit specification of a shared conceptualisation of a domain. Relations — relatedTo: Knowledge Graph.
Semantic Web. An extension of the web in which data is given well-defined, machine-readable meaning.

Vector Database. A database optimised for similarity search over high-dimensional embedding vectors. Is a kind of: Data Structure. Vector databases index dense embeddings for approximate nearest-neighbour search; the trade-off is recall for latency.
